runs.text: Premium Online Learning & Entrepreneur Community Platform
Three Functional Modules on a Shared Platform Architecture | Single Integrated Delivery

rows: 45-60 calendar days; three functional modules delivered together on one shared platform

runs.text: Prepared for client review based on the supplied Premium Online Learning Platform Project SOP and its marked exclusions.

This SOW converts the client-provided Premium Online Learning Platform Project SOP into an implementation-ready plan for the project named Preneur Gate. The scope has been reorganized into three interconnected modules to simplify delivery ownership, sequencing, quality assurance and final acceptance.

body.text: The Website & Member Experience, Course & E-Book Learning Platform, and Admin Management Platform will be developed in parallel wherever technically feasible. Internal demonstrations may occur during development, but no module will be treated as a separate final delivery. All three modules will be integrated, tested and delivered together as one product.

items.text: Features visibly crossed out in red in the supplied SOP are excluded from this SOW.

Where the SOP retains a high-level capability but crosses out a related dashboard widget or sub-feature, the retained capability is included only within the boundaries explicitly described in this SOW.
Features that are described as conditional in the supplied SOP, but do not define implementation details, are not treated as committed base-scope integrations unless expressly listed here.
Technology stack, hosting provider, commercial values, payment terms and final production infrastructure are not specified in the source SOP and therefore remain to be mutually confirmed.

runs.text: Preneur Gate will be developed as a premium online education and entrepreneur community platform combining structured learning, digital reading, assessments, AI-assisted study support, professional member networking and centralized administration.

The implementation will be organized as three parallel product modules so that public/member experience, learning delivery and administration can progress concurrently while sharing a common authentication, permissions, data and design foundation.

items.text: Provide secure user registration, authentication and personalized onboarding.
Provide a learner dashboard showing enrolled learning, progress, assessments, certificates, community activity and notifications within the retained scope.
Deliver recorded/video learning with progress tracking, resume capability, lesson navigation and enrollment/permission-based access.
Deliver an interactive in-browser e-book reading experience with bookmarks, highlighting, notes, search and reading-progress tracking.
Provide AI-assisted study functions for course and e-book learning, excluding the crossed-out entrepreneur-focused AI assistance.
Provide mock tests, assessments, results, performance metrics and retained leaderboard functionality.
Provide digital certificates with verification-oriented fields retained in the SOP.
Provide entrepreneur community profiles, feeds, connections, groups, geo-based member discovery and member interactions.
Provide centralized admin controls for users, learning content, assessments, community moderation, certificates, website content and platform analytics.
Provide a premium, modern, minimal, responsive user experience across desktop, laptop, tablet and mobile browsers.

body.text: The three modules are not sequential phase deliveries. Development, review and QA will be parallelized, followed by one integrated UAT and one combined production delivery. The contractual implementation window should be read as 45-60 calendar days from formal commencement, subject to the response times stated in this SOW.

blocks.text: 2.1 Architecture Principle - Three Functional Modules, One Shared Platform

runs.text: Preneur Gate will use three functional/product modules for planning, ownership and acceptance; technically, these modules will operate on a shared platform architecture rather than as three independent backends. This prevents duplication of users, permissions, course data, learning progress, community data, assessments and analytics.

items.text: Single user identity and authentication foundation across all modules.
Role-based permissions and access control used consistently by learner/community and admin interfaces.
Shared data model for users, courses, e-books, assessments, certificates, community objects and analytics.
Shared responsive component system and premium visual language.
Common notification and activity data where required by retained features.
Integrated search across retained searchable entities.

body.text: Use a modular-monolith core backend with clear domain boundaries, a unified user-facing web application, a separate administration frontend, a shared relational data layer, object/media storage, cache, search interfaces and an isolated AI/RAG integration layer. This pattern is intentionally chosen to support the 45-60 day delivery window while preserving a clean path to future scale-out.

runs.text: The frontend architecture will use two deployable applications while preserving the three functional SOW modules.

items.text: User Web Application: public website, authentication/onboarding, learner dashboard, Course & E-Book Learning experiences, AI Student Buddy, assessments, certificates, community, profiles, groups, geo discovery, goals and search.

Admin Web Application: a separate administration interface for authorized administrators to manage users, roles, permissions, courses, e-books, assessments, community moderation, certificates, CMS content and platform analytics.
The Course & E-Book Learning module will live inside the same user web experience rather than requiring learners to move between unrelated applications or duplicated accounts.
A shared design/component system will keep visual behavior consistent across public, member and admin surfaces while allowing admin-specific interaction patterns.

blocks.text: 2.3 API & Core Backend Layer - Modular Monolith

runs.text: The initial release should use one deployable core backend organized into well-defined domain modules. Each domain remains logically separated in code and permissions, but the platform avoids premature microservice complexity.

items.text: Primary relational database: one shared transactional database is recommended for the first release (PostgreSQL or equivalent), with data logically separated by domain rather than duplicated per product module.
Cache / short-lived state: Redis or an equivalent cache is recommended for rate limits, temporary tokens, frequently accessed data and other transient platform state where appropriate.
Object storage: videos, PDFs, e-books, profile images, community media and course attachments should be stored in object/file storage rather than inside the relational database.
CDN/media delivery: large media assets should be delivered through a CDN or managed media-delivery layer to avoid routing heavy file traffic through the business API.
Private/protected learning assets must remain subject to backend authorization/entitlement checks or secure access mechanisms.

runs.text: The core backend will control who is allowed to access learning media and will store progress/completion state; large video delivery itself should be handled by a storage/CDN or managed streaming layer.

items.text: Reader state is a first-class application domain rather than a simple file viewer.
The backend will retain reading position/progress, bookmarks, highlights, notes and download permissions for supported e-book content.
The user web app will provide the in-browser reading interface and synchronization of learner state.
AI actions on book content will be routed through the protected AI layer rather than directly from the browser to an AI vendor.

runs.text: AI functionality should be isolated behind a Preneur Gate AI service/orchestration layer. The browser will call Preneur Gate APIs; API keys and AI-provider access will not be exposed to end users.

items.text: The AI layer will enforce user authorization, usage controls, prompt/context structure, logging and provider abstraction.

Course/e-book-aware assistance should retrieve relevant authorized learning content before generating responses (RAG/retrieval-based context), so the AI can ground explanations and summaries in the learner content available to that user.
A vector/search index may be introduced for course/e-book chunks when required by the final AI implementation. The exact provider/database remains a technical implementation decision.
Third-party AI model/API charges remain outside the software build unless separately included commercially, consistent with the source scope.

Search will be exposed through a shared Search API/service boundary. The first release may use relational full-text/indexed search; a dedicated search engine can be introduced later without changing the user-facing contract.
Notifications will be centralized through a Notification module so course, assessment, certificate and community features do not implement unrelated notification logic separately.

Key business activities (for example course completion, assessment submission, certificate issuance and community activity) should generate structured activity events that can feed retained analytics and dashboards.

runs.text: The recommended first-release deployment topology is deliberately simple and production-oriented:

items.text: Single Core API / Backend deployment (modular monolith).
AI/RAG integration service or isolated backend module with separate provider credentials.
Environment-specific configuration for development/staging/production as agreed.

runs.text: The architecture is designed to avoid over-engineering the first release while retaining clear extraction points. If scale, operational load or team ownership later requires independent services, high-load capabilities can be separated without redesigning the product modules.

header: ARCHITECTURE DECISION SUMMARYPreneur Gate is commercially organized as three modules, but technically implemented as two frontends (User Web + Admin Web) connected to one shared modular core platform. This creates one source of truth for identity, permissions and business data, supports the agreed single combined launch, reduces delivery risk within 45-60 days, and keeps future scalability options open.

body.text: Preneur Gate will be delivered as one integrated product consisting of all three in-scope modules. Module-level completion does not trigger independent final acceptance; the release milestone is the integrated production-ready product after combined QA and UAT.
